title: Fire Safety Violations: Penalties for Homes and Businesses 2026
desc: 2026 fire prevention penalties for households and businesses under Decree 106/2025 as amended by 69/2026: electrical faults, escape routes, extinguishers.
summary: Common fire safety violations in homes and business premises and the corresponding fines under Decree 106/2025/ND-CP as amended by Decree 69/2026/ND-CP.
body: p

Administrative penalties for violations of fire prevention, firefighting, and rescue rules are governed by Decree 106/2025/ND-CP (effective 1 July 2025), as amended by Decree 69/2026/ND-CP (effective 20 April 2026). Below are the violations that homeowners and business households most often commit.
h2
1. Maximum fines and who is penalized
ul
The maximum fine for an individual is VND 50 million; an organization committing the same violation is fined twice as much (Article 4).
Households and business households are subject to the same fines as individuals. The amounts below are the amounts for individuals.
A person who rents, borrows, or stays in a house is penalized in line with their own fire safety responsibility (Clause 7, Article 3, added by Article 2 of Decree 69/2026).
h2
2. Electrical and open-flame violations
ul
Installing or using electric wires, electrical equipment, switching devices, or protection devices that are not fire-safe: VND 6–8 million (Clause 1, Article 12).
No fire-containment measures for a centralized indoor electric vehicle charging area: VND 40–50 million, plus a requirement to implement fire-containment measures (Clauses 4 and 6, Article 12).
Using a flame or heat source without the required fire-safety distance: VND 5–10 million; welding or cutting metal without fire safety measures: VND 20–25 million (Article 11).
p

Violations involving electric wires and equipment (Clause 1, Article 12) and the use of flame sources, welding, and cutting (Article 11) are fined double if they cause a fire (not serious enough for criminal prosecution); the electric vehicle charging violation in Clause 4 is not subject to this doubling.
h2
3. Escape route violations
p
Under Article 24 (amended by Article 11 of Decree 69/2026):
ul
Installing mirrors on an escape route, or doors on escape exits that do not open in the direction of escape: VND 1–3 million.
Leaving goods, vehicles, or objects that obstruct an escape route: VND 5–10 million, plus a requirement to remove them.

Failing to maintain, or not having, adequate escape routes for a room or area: VND 20–30 million; for a house or building: VND 40–50 million. Not having adequate escape routes for a house or building also results in suspension of operations for 1 to 3 months.
h2
4. Fire extinguisher and fire alarm violations
ul

Failing to provide common firefighting equipment (fire extinguishers, etc.) or basic demolition tools: VND 3–5 million; providing equipment that does not meet regulations: VND 1–2 million (Clauses 1 and 2, Article 20).
Moving or obscuring fire safety equipment without authorization: VND 1–3 million (Clause 1, Article 21).

Failing to maintain the required number and technical standards of installed fire extinguishers, or failing to maintain firefighting water reserves: VND 3–5 million (Clause 2, Article 21, amended by Article 9 of Decree 69/2026).
Failing to keep an installed standalone fire alarm working: VND 5–10 million (Point b, Clause 3, Article 21).
h2
5. Flammable and explosive goods, and fire and explosion insurance
ul

Storing fire- or explosion-hazardous substances and goods in a way that does not meet regulations, or storing quantities above the limit: VND 3–5 million; storing or using them outside designated places: VND 5–10 million (Clauses 1 and 2, Article 14).
Failing to buy mandatory fire and explosion insurance where a facility is required to have it: VND 30–40 million (Group 2 facilities) or VND 40–50 million (Group 1 facilities) (Article 17).
h2
6. Who imposes penalties, and the limitation period
p

The Chairperson of the commune-level People's Committee may impose fines of up to VND 25 million and temporary suspension of operations (Clause 1, Article 30, amended by Article 14 of Decree 69/2026). The limitation period for penalties is 1 year (Article 5). To avoid penalties, see the requirements in Fire safety requirements for houses 2026 and Home-cum-business premises: fire safety conditions.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. Decree 106/2025/ND-CP is partially no longer in force because it has been amended by Decree 69/2026/ND-CP; this article has been checked against the amended articles. Acts that occurred and ended before 20 April 2026 are governed by the rules in force at the time of the violation (Article 24 of Decree 69/2026).
